evidence.approach:
One source file and a generator. docs/harness/skill.md holds the skill's body: the five stages with the command for each, the three rules a session cannot infer, and a pointer to this ticket's journal as the worked example. harness/skills.py writes each copy as a generated header plus that body, where the header carries the YAML frontmatter each assistant reads (name seen-harness, and a description saying when it applies) and a line saying the file is generated from docs/harness/skill.md and must not be edited. sync writes .claude/skills/seen-harness/SKILL.md and .agents/skills/seen-harness/SKILL.md in the project, and ~/.codex/skills/seen-harness/SKILL.md when that directory already exists, because that is where Codex reads one. doctor compares the two committed copies against what the generator would write and reports drift without repairing it, the same stance it takes on everything else; the copy outside the repository is a machine's own business and is not checked.

The workflow document and CLAUDE.md are then corrected against the harness that exists: the command table, the delivered stage, reopen and the merge check, the coverage gate, the conventions the tickets established, and the calibrated threshold.
changes: docs/harness/skill.md: new, the single maintained skill body
harness/skills.py: new, render() building a copy from the body and sync() writing them
harness/doctor.py: drift between each committed copy and what the generator would write
harness/paths.py: the skill source and its two committed targets
docs/harness/workflow.md: corrected to the harness as built
CLAUDE.md: the command list as it now is
harness/tests/test_skill.py: new, generation, drift and the frontmatter each assistant needs
tests_first: sync writes both committed copies from the source, each carrying name and description in frontmatter and a line naming its source: the RED must fail because no skills module exists
doctor reports drift when a copy is edited by hand, naming the file, and repairs nothing: the RED must fail for the same reason
doctor passes immediately after sync, so a clean tree is quiet: the RED must fail for the same reason
sync writes the Codex copy outside the repository only when that directory already exists, and never creates it: the RED must fail because nothing writes there
alternatives: Committing each copy by hand, rejected because two files that must agree and are edited separately will not agree
doctor repairing drift, rejected because a silent repair hides what a reviewer needs to see
Creating ~/.codex when it does not exist, rejected because a repository command should not install things on a machine that has not asked
risks: A skill read before every ticket competes for the context the ticket needs, so the body stays short and points at the workflow document for detail
The Codex copy outside the repository can drift silently, which doctor cannot see; sync rewrites it whenever it runs, and the ticket says so rather than implying coverage it does not have
evidence.rollback: Revert the commit and delete the generated copies. Nothing else reads them.
